chapters.title: Outcomes of Democracy
chapters.summary: In this chapter: how should we assess democracy’s outcomes?; accountable, responsive and legitimate government; economic growth and development; reduction of inequality and poverty.

lessons.title: How should we assess democracy’s outcomes?

activities.prompt: How can we judge whether democracy truly works for people?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: What democracy can offer
activities.body: Democracy is considered better than dictatorship and other alternatives. It is expected to promote equality among citizens. It can also enhance each person's dignity. It can improve decisions and help resolve conflicts. It leaves room for correcting mistakes. These are expected benefits, not guarantees. Democracies differ in social situations, economic achievements and cultures. More than a hundred countries claim and practise some democratic politics.
keyPoints: Democracy is considered better than dictatorship and other alternatives.
Democracy is expected to support equality, dignity and better decisions.
Democracies vary across social situations, economic achievements and cultures.
activities.explanation: These points describe democracy’s expected benefits and differences.

activities.prompt: Two classmates want different playground rules. How should their class decide?
steps: Both classmates should speak because democracy values equal treatment.
They should vote because democracy gives people a way to resolve conflicts.
A wrong rule can change because democracy leaves room for correcting mistakes.
Everyone should help improve the rule because democracy cannot achieve goals alone.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Democracy and citizen action
activities.body: Democracy is only one form of government. It cannot achieve goals by itself. However, it can create conditions in which goals may be achieved. Citizens must use these conditions to achieve their goals. This means citizens have an important role. Democratic benefits are expected outcomes, not automatic results.
keyPoints: Democracy cannot achieve goals by itself.
It can create conditions where goals may be achieved.
Citizens must use those conditions to achieve their goals.
activities.explanation: Democratic conditions can support goals, but citizens must use them.

activities.prompt: Which outcome is democracy expected to promote?
options: Equality among citizens
Fewer public choices
One shared culture
A fixed social situation
activities.explanation: Democracy is expected to promote equality among citizens.

activities.prompt: Democracy is considered better than dictatorship and other alternatives.
activities.explanation: The lesson presents democracy as the better option among these forms of government.

activities.prompt: Democracy gives people a ______ for resolving conflicts.
activities.hint: Think about how people can settle disagreements.
activities.explanation: A method gives citizens a way to resolve conflicts peacefully.

activities.prompt: Match each outcome with its role in democracy.
activities.explanation: Democracy is expected to promote equality, dignity and better decisions.

activities.prompt: Put these steps in order for using democracy to achieve goals.
activities.explanation: Democracy creates conditions, and citizens must use them to achieve their goals.

activities.prompt: Which statement best matches the lesson’s view of democracy?
options: Democracy can create conditions for achieving goals.
Democracy guarantees every shared goal.
Government alone can achieve all goals.
Citizens do not need to use democratic conditions.
activities.explanation: Democracy can create useful conditions, but citizens must use them to achieve goals.

activities.prompt: A town votes on a public plan. People disagree before the vote. What can democracy do here?
options: It can settle the disagreement through a peaceful method.
It can make every citizen agree with the final decision.
It can guarantee that the public plan will succeed.
It can remove the need for citizens to use its conditions.

why.It can make every citizen agree with the: This mistake assumes that voting forces everyone to agree.
why.It can guarantee that the public plan wi: This mistake assumes that democracy guarantees success.
why.It can remove the need for citizens to u: This mistake forgets that citizens must use democratic conditions.

activities.explanation: This is right because voting offers a peaceful way to resolve conflict.

activities.prompt: One town has a different social situation. Another has different economic results and cultures. What should a fair comparison of their democracies remember?
options: They may have different results because their situations are different.
One democracy must always have better economic results.
All democracies must produce the same results in every culture.
Only economic achievements can explain differences between democracies.

why.One democracy must always have better ec: This mistake treats one place's results as a universal rule.
why.All democracies must produce the same re: This mistake assumes all democracies must have identical results.
why.Only economic achievements can explain d: This mistake ignores social and cultural differences.

activities.explanation: This is right because their social, economic and cultural situations differ.

activities.prompt: At a meeting, two families argue about park hours. Residents vote and follow the result. Why might they act this way?
options: Democracy gives them a peaceful way to settle disputes.
They believe voting makes every family truly equal.
They think the government should decide every park matter.
They want no chance to change a later decision.

why.They believe voting makes every family t: This mistake confuses equal treatment with identical opinions.
why.They think the government should decide: This mistake assumes government alone should make every decision.
why.They want no chance to change a later de: This mistake thinks democracy removes any chance of correction.

activities.explanation: This is right because voting is a democratic method for resolving conflicts.

activities.prompt: At first, a school vote supports one rule. Later, students change it after discussing problems. What does this change show?
options: Democracy can correct mistakes through discussion and another decision.
Democracy prevents citizens from disagreeing at the start.
Every first decision must already be perfectly fair.
Changing a decision means democracy has stopped working.

why.Democracy prevents citizens from disagre: This mistake thinks democracy prevents all early disagreement.
why.Every first decision must already be per: This mistake assumes a first vote must always be perfect.
why.Changing a decision means democracy has: This mistake treats changing a decision as the end of democracy.

activities.explanation: This is right because democracy allows room to correct mistakes.

lessons.title: Accountable, responsive and legitimate government

activities.prompt: How can we make our government more accountable, responsive, and legitimate?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: What makes democratic government accountable?
activities.body: Democratic government means government by the people. It follows accepted norms and procedures, so decisions may take more time. Such decisions may be more acceptable and effective. Governments are accountable to the people and respond to citizens’ needs. Transparency lets citizens examine decisions. Citizens should participate and know what the government is doing. Legitimate means rightly accepted as the people’s own government. Democracies have a mixed record and face corruption.
keyPoints: Democratic procedures can make decisions more acceptable and effective.
Democratic governments must be accountable, responsive and legitimate.
Citizens should participate, examine decisions and receive information.
activities.explanation: A strong democracy makes government answerable to citizens.

activities.prompt: The local council wants new playground rules. How should it decide so people trust the result?
steps: The council follows agreed steps because democratic decisions depend on accepted procedures.
It shares how the choice was made because transparency lets citizens examine it.
It listens and includes residents because it must be accountable and responsive to them.
The council's democratic choice is legitimate because it is the people's own government.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Which meaning best matches transparency?
options: Let citizens examine decisions
Make decisions without delay
Keep government work secret
Choose only one leader
activities.explanation: Transparency means citizens can examine how decisions were made.

activities.prompt: Transparency lets citizens ______ how decisions were made.
activities.hint: Look closely at the steps.
activities.explanation: Transparency means citizens can examine how decisions were made.

activities.prompt: Match each government quality to its meaning.
activities.explanation: These qualities help citizens trust and understand democratic government.

activities.prompt: Why can democratic procedures improve decisions?
options: They may be more acceptable and effective.
They always finish without waiting.
They remove the need for citizens.
They make procedures unnecessary.
activities.explanation: Decisions made through democratic procedures may be more acceptable and effective.

activities.prompt: Put these parts of democratic decision-making in order.
items: Citizens examine how it was made
activities.explanation: Democratic decisions use accepted norms and procedures. Citizens can then examine how decisions were made.

activities.prompt: Which pair are signs of a healthy democracy?
options: Free and fair elections and open debate
Secret votes and closed debates
One leader makes every important choice
Decisions are made without procedures
activities.explanation: Free and fair elections and open public debate are signs of a healthy democracy.

activities.prompt: A council delays a decision because it follows agreed steps. What is likely to happen?
options: The decision may be more accepted and effective.
The council will please every resident equally.
The council can skip checks after the delay.
The public will stop asking about the result.

why.The council will please every resident e: Democratic decisions do not guarantee that everyone will like them.
why.The council can skip checks after the de: Procedures are still needed after a delay.
why.The public will stop asking about the re: A delay does not remove citizens' right to information.

activities.explanation: Following procedures can make decisions more acceptable and effective.

activities.prompt: Place A lets residents see each step before a decision. Place B hides the reasons. What difference does this create?
options: Place A is transparent because residents can examine the decision.
Place A is legitimate because every resident agrees with it.
Place B is accountable because it keeps its reasons secret.
Place A is corruption-free because it shows each step.

why.Place A is legitimate because every resi: Legitimacy comes from the government being the people's own.
why.Place B is accountable because it keeps: Accountability means answering to people, not hiding decisions.
why.Place A is corruption-free because it sh: Showing steps gives transparency, but it cannot remove corruption.

activities.explanation: Transparency lets citizens examine how a decision was made.

activities.prompt: Residents say buses stop too early. The council changes its plan after listening. Which government duty is shown?
options: Responsiveness, because it acted on citizens' needs.
Transparency, because it showed every meeting detail.
Legitimacy, because buses now stop at the right time.
Accountability, because residents checked the council's records.

why.Transparency, because it showed every me: Showing meeting details shows transparency, not responsiveness.
why.Legitimacy, because buses now stop at th: Legitimacy comes from the government being the people's own.
why.Accountability, because residents checke: Checking records shows transparency; accountability means answering to people.

activities.explanation: Responsiveness means acting on the needs and expectations of citizens.

activities.prompt: The council will close the local park. It invites residents before deciding. Why is this important?
options: It lets citizens join a decision that affects them.
It guarantees that every proposed closure will succeed.
It removes the council's duty to follow procedures.
It proves that the council is free from corruption.

why.It guarantees that every proposed closur: Participation helps decisions, but it does not guarantee every outcome.
why.It removes the council's duty to follow: Citizen input does not cancel the council's procedural duties.
why.It proves that the council is free from: One meeting cannot prove that corruption is completely absent.

activities.explanation: Citizens should have ways to participate in decisions that affect them.

activities.prompt: After a fair election, a report says an official accepted money from a bidder. What can we conclude?
options: Democracy can exist even when corruption is present.
The election must be unfair because one official broke a rule.
Open debate should end after any wrongdoing appears.
Democratic procedures always prevent corruption in government.

why.The election must be unfair because one: One official's wrongdoing does not prove that the election was unfair.
why.Open debate should end after any wrongdo: Corruption by one official does not mean open debate must end.
why.Democratic procedures always prevent cor: Democratic procedures do not make corruption completely impossible.

activities.explanation: Democracy is not completely free from corruption.

lessons.title: Economic growth and development

activities.prompt: Can democracy help a country grow without promising it will?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Growth, development and democracy
activities.body: Economic growth is the rate used to compare democracies and dictatorships. Economic development is what democracies may be expected to produce through good governments. Many democracies did not meet this expectation. Dictatorships had slightly higher overall growth. This failure causes concern. The growth result alone cannot reject democracy. Economic development depends on several factors. Democracy cannot guarantee development. Yet it can be expected to avoid falling behind dictatorships in growth.
keyPoints: Democracies may reasonably be expected to produce development.
Dictatorships had slightly higher overall economic growth.
Growth results alone cannot reject democracy.
activities.explanation: This shows why growth results need careful study.

activities.prompt: A family hears that dictatorships grow faster. Should they stop supporting democracy?
steps: People may expect democracies to develop because they can produce good governments.
Many democracies did not meet this expectation, and dictatorships had slightly higher overall growth.
However, democracy cannot guarantee economic development, because development depends on several factors.
Growth alone is not a reason to reject democracy, so the family should not stop supporting it.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: A balanced view
activities.body: Democracy's failure to achieve higher economic development causes concern. This does not mean the growth result alone should reject democracy. Poor dictatorships and democracies had almost the same development rate. Economic development depends on several different factors. Democracy cannot guarantee development. However, democracy can be expected to avoid falling behind dictatorships in economic growth.
keyPoints: Democratic development failure causes concern.
Poor dictatorships and democracies had almost equal development rates.
Democracy can avoid falling behind in economic growth.
activities.explanation: This is a balanced view of democracy and growth.

activities.prompt: Many democracies fulfilled the expectation of economic development.
activities.explanation: Many democracies did not fulfil the expectation of economic development.

activities.prompt: What may people reasonably expect democracies to produce when they make good governments?
options: economic development
higher economic growth
lower economic growth
equal economic growth
activities.explanation: The lesson connects good governments with a reasonable expectation of development.

activities.prompt: Many democracies did not fulfil the expectation of ______ development.
activities.hint: The lesson links this word with expected outcomes from good governments.
activities.explanation: Many democracies did not fulfil the expectation of economic development.

activities.prompt: Match each phrase with its correct connection.
pairs: Not a reason to reject democracy
activities.explanation: Each pair matches a finding or conclusion stated in the lesson.

activities.prompt: Which group had a slightly higher rate of economic growth overall?
options: Overall, dictatorships had the higher rate
Overall, democracies had the higher rate
Poorer democracies had the higher rate
Poorer dictatorships had the higher rate
activities.explanation: The lesson says dictatorships had a slightly higher rate overall.

activities.prompt: Democracy can be expected to avoid falling behind dictatorships in economic growth.
activities.explanation: Democracy can be expected to avoid falling behind dictatorships in economic growth.

activities.prompt: Which conclusion about democracy and economic development is best supported?
options: Development is possible, but not guaranteed
Development is guaranteed in every democracy
Democracy should be rejected using growth results
Democracy should always produce higher growth
activities.explanation: People may reasonably expect development, but democracy cannot guarantee it. Growth results alone cannot reject democracy.

activities.prompt: Two poorer countries have different governments. Their growth-rate difference is negligible. What does this suggest?
options: Government type barely explains the difference.
Government type explains all the difference.
Both countries must grow at exactly the same rate.
Democracies always grow faster in poorer countries.

why.Government type explains all the differe: This makes a small difference sound complete.
why.Both countries must grow at exactly the: Negligible difference does not mean the rates must be identical.
why.Democracies always grow faster in poorer: This turns a small comparison into an always-true rule.

activities.explanation: This matches the negligible difference found in poorer countries.

activities.prompt: A map shows poorer democracies and poorer dictatorships. Their growth rates are nearly equal. What can the map show?
options: Government type makes little difference here.
Government type makes every difference.
Democracies cannot grow at all.
Dictatorships must grow faster everywhere.

This treats a small difference as if it explained everything.
Equal rates do not mean democracies have no growth.
why.Dictatorships must grow faster everywher: One map cannot support a rule about everywhere.

activities.explanation: The nearly equal rates support a small difference, not a large one.

lessons.sceneCaption: Good roads connect rural communities and support economic development.

lessons.title: Reduction of inequality and poverty

activities.prompt: How can a democracy become fairer when some people still live in poverty?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Equal votes, unequal wealth
activities.body: Democracies give people equal political weight when choosing representatives. Yet economic inequality can grow as political participation becomes more equal. A small number of ultra-rich people receive a highly disproportionate share of wealth and income. Meanwhile, lower incomes can decline, and some poor people cannot meet basic needs. Poor people often form a large share of voters. Therefore, reducing economic disparities remains an important democratic challenge.
keyPoints: Every person has equal weight in elections.
Economic inequality can grow despite political equality.
Poor people form a large share of voters.
activities.explanation: Equal political weight does not automatically produce economic equality.

activities.prompt: In a country, every adult has one vote. Yet some people at the bottom cannot meet basic needs. Why can both happen?
steps: Democracy is based on political equality, so every person has equal voting weight.
Economic inequalities can still grow while political participation becomes more equal.
As bottom incomes decline, some poor people cannot meet basic needs.
Therefore, democracies have not been very successful in reducing economic inequalities.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Why Democracies Face This Challenge
activities.body: Political equality means that each person's vote counts equally when representatives are chosen. However, democracy has not reduced economic inequalities very successfully. Wealth and income can become sharply unequal. Lower-income groups may lose income, while some poor people lack food, housing, education and health. Because poor citizens often make up a large voting group, democracies can reasonably be expected to narrow economic disparities.
keyPoints: Each person's vote counts equally.
Poor citizens form a large voting group.
Democracies can reasonably be expected to reduce disparities.
activities.explanation: Poor voters have strong political weight, but economic inequality remains a serious challenge.

activities.title: Equal Political Weight
activities.prompt: What does political equality mean when representatives are elected?
options: Wealth decides who has more weight.
Every person has equal weight.
Only some people receive political weight.
Rich people receive extra weight.
activities.explanation: Every person has equal weight when electing representatives.

activities.title: Political Equality and Inequality
activities.prompt: Economic inequalities must fall when political participation becomes more equal.
activities.explanation: They can grow even as political participation becomes more equal. Political equality does not guarantee economic equality.

activities.title: A Basic Need
activities.prompt: Some poor people cannot meet basic needs such as food, clothing, housing, ______ and health.
activities.hint: This need helps people gain knowledge and skills.
activities.explanation: Education is one of the basic needs that some poor people cannot meet.

activities.title: Match Each Description
activities.prompt: Match each group or idea with its description.
pairs: A highly disproportionate share of wealth and income
Limited success in reducing economic inequalities
activities.explanation: Each pair connects a group with what the lesson says about it.

activities.title: Two Kinds of Equality
activities.prompt: Which statement best describes the relationship between political and economic equality?
options: Economic inequality can grow despite political equality.
Economic inequality must shrink with political equality.
Economic inequality always ends with political equality.
Economic inequality cannot exist with political equality.
activities.explanation: Economic inequalities can grow even while political participation becomes more equal.

activities.title: The Unequal Outcome
activities.prompt: Which evidence best shows the tension between political equality and economic inequality?
options: Votes have equal weight, but a few receive a disproportionate wealth share.
Votes have unequal weight, but a few receive an equal wealth share.
Votes have equal weight, and everyone receives an equal wealth share.
Votes have unequal weight, and everyone receives an equal wealth share.
activities.explanation: Every person has equal electoral weight. Yet a small number receive a highly disproportionate share of wealth and income.

activities.prompt: A country gives all adults equal voting weight. A few ultra-rich people then gain a larger share of wealth. What can happen?
options: Economic inequality can grow while voting becomes more equal.
Political equality must stop economic inequality immediately.
Equal voting weight means every person has equal wealth.
Ultra-rich people receive more voting weight than others.

why.Political equality must stop economic in: This wrongly assumes that political equality immediately removes economic inequality.
why.Equal voting weight means every person h: This wrongly assumes that equal voting weight guarantees equal wealth.
why.Ultra-rich people receive more voting we: This wrongly assumes that greater wealth produces greater voting weight.

activities.explanation: This is right because economic inequalities can grow even with more equal political participation.

activities.prompt: A map shows over half of Bangladesh’s population living in poverty. Which group can this help us understand?
options: People who always receive the same wealth share.
People who are guaranteed to own large comfortable homes.
People who always have the strongest voting power.
People who may struggle to meet basic needs.

why.People who always receive the same wealt: This wrongly suggests that poverty guarantees everyone an equal wealth share.
why.People who are guaranteed to own large c: This wrongly suggests that poverty guarantees large and comfortable homes.
why.People who always have the strongest vot: This wrongly suggests that poverty gives people the strongest political power.

activities.explanation: This is right because some poor people cannot meet basic needs.

activities.prompt: Poor people form a large group of voters in many democracies. They reasonably expect representatives to reduce economic disparities. Why has this expectation not led to success?
options: Most poor voters secretly support greater inequality.
Equal political weight has not reduced economic inequality much.
Representatives must ignore the demands of poor voters.
Reducing disparities requires giving rich people more votes.

why.Most poor voters secretly support greate: This wrongly suggests that poor voters support greater economic inequality.
why.Representatives must ignore the demands: This wrongly assumes that representatives should ignore poor voters’ demands.
why.Reducing disparities requires giving ric: This wrongly assumes that richer people should receive more voting weight.

activities.explanation: This is right because democracies have not been very successful in reducing economic inequalities.

activities.prompt: The incomes of people at the bottom of society keep falling. What effect can this have on poor people’s lives?
options: Some poor people may gain secure food and housing.
Some poor people may become richer than the ultra-rich.
Some poor people may fail to meet basic needs.
Some poor people may gain much stronger voting power.

why.Some poor people may gain secure food an: This wrongly assumes that falling incomes improve poor people’s basic lives.
why.Some poor people may become richer than: This wrongly assumes that declining bottom incomes can surpass ultra-rich wealth.
why.Some poor people may gain much stronger: This wrongly assumes that falling income automatically increases voting weight.

activities.explanation: This is right because declining incomes can leave some poor people unable to meet basic needs.

lessons.title: Accommodation of social diversity

activities.prompt: How can we learn to live together when people see the world differently?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Living with social differences
activities.body: Democracy can help produce a harmonious social life and handle social conflicts. It can develop procedures for competition. These procedures reduce the chance of tensions becoming explosive or violent. People can learn to respect differences and negotiate them. A majority must work with the minority. Majority rule must not become the rule of one religious, racial or language community. No society can completely and permanently resolve conflicts between different groups.
keyPoints: Democratic procedures can reduce violent social tensions.
People can learn respect and negotiate social differences.
Majorities must work with minorities.
activities.explanation: These ideas show how democracy can manage social differences and conflicts.

activities.prompt: How should a democratic town decide when one group has more supporters?
steps: A majority's power needs limits, because no community should rule alone.
Open competition is useful because it gives groups agreed ways to compete.
Groups can negotiate differences, because this reduces the chance of violent conflict.
Thus, majority rule must include minorities so government represents the general view.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: What can we fairly expect democracy to produce?
options: A society without conflicts
Rule by one community
A harmonious social life
A permanent end to group conflict
activities.explanation: Democracy can produce a harmonious social life. It cannot completely and permanently remove every conflict.

activities.prompt: Democracies usually develop ______ for conducting competition.
activities.hint: These help guide competition fairly.
activities.explanation: Democracies usually develop procedures for conducting competition.

activities.prompt: Match each idea to its lesson meaning.
pairs: Reduce the chance of violent tensions
activities.explanation: Belgium shows successful negotiation. Procedures can reduce violent tensions, and majorities must work with minorities.

activities.prompt: What can people learn to do with social differences?
options: End every group conflict
Respect social differences
Choose one social group
Stop respecting social differences
activities.explanation: People can learn to respect social differences. Societies can also develop ways to negotiate them.

activities.prompt: What can democratic procedures do to social tensions?
options: Increase the chance of violence
Remove every group conflict
Reduce the chance of violence
End every group difference
activities.explanation: These procedures reduce the chance of social tensions becoming explosive or violent.

activities.prompt: What should every citizen have a chance of?
options: Leading the majority all the time
Belonging to a majority at some time
Belonging to one community always
Choosing one language for ever
activities.explanation: Every citizen should have a chance of belonging to a majority at some time.

activities.prompt: A democracy uses agreed competition procedures. Why can this support a harmonious social life?
options: Competition procedures can stop tensions from becoming violent.
Every social disagreement will disappear for ever.
One community will control every public decision.
People will learn to respect every social difference.

why.Every social disagreement will disappear: This wrongly assumes that every social conflict can disappear for ever.
why.One community will control every public: This confuses majority rule with control by one community.
why.People will learn to respect every socia: People can learn respect, but these procedures do not guarantee it.

activities.explanation: These procedures reduce the chance of tensions becoming explosive or violent.

activities.prompt: Belgium successfully negotiated differences among ethnic populations. Another society lets one ethnic community rule alone. Which comparison fits the facts?
options: Belgium shows negotiation; the other society shows domination.
Both show that one community can rule in a fair way.
Belgium shows that democracy ends every conflict for ever.
The other society shows that minorities must never be heard.

why.Both show that one community can rule in: This wrongly treats domination by one community as fair government.
why.Belgium shows that democracy ends every: This wrongly assumes that democracy can solve every conflict for ever.
why.The other society shows that minorities: This wrongly treats excluding minorities as a democratic solution.

activities.explanation: Belgium shows successful negotiation, while one-community rule breaks democratic inclusion.

activities.prompt: A town map shows different language communities living together. What does this suggest for government?
options: Government should help every group negotiate their differences.
The larger group should make every decision alone.
The map proves that all conflict has already ended.
Only one community needs to take part in decisions.

why.The larger group should make every decis: This confuses a larger group with a right to rule alone.
why.The map proves that all conflict has alr: A map of where people live cannot prove that conflict has ended.
why.Only one community needs to take part in: This wrongly excludes one community from democratic decisions.

activities.explanation: The map shows shared life, so government should help groups negotiate.

activities.prompt: A religious community wins most votes, but others also live there. Which action follows the rule of majority rule?
options: The majority should work with minority groups.
The winning community should rule without any limits.
The minority should never join public decisions.
Government should represent only the winning community.

why.The winning community should rule withou: Majority rule must not become rule by one religious community.
why.The minority should never join public de: This wrongly excludes minority citizens from government decisions.
why.Government should represent only the win: Government should represent the general view, not one community alone.

activities.explanation: Working with minorities helps government represent the general view.

activities.prompt: A child belongs to a small language group. Which democratic idea gives every citizen hope over time?
options: Every citizen should get a chance to be in a majority.
The current minority should always stay outside power.
Only one community should ever gain majority status.
The present majority should keep power for ever.

why.The current minority should always stay: This wrongly treats minority status as permanent political exclusion.
why.Only one community should ever gain majo: This wrongly gives one community permanent majority status.
why.The present majority should keep power f: This wrongly assumes that present majorities should rule for ever.

activities.explanation: Every citizen should have a chance to belong to a majority at some time.

activities.prompt: A democracy is used to handle conflict between social groups. Why is this especially suitable, and what should leaders remember?
options: It supports negotiation and respect, but conflicts never disappear for ever.
It can remove every conflict once and for all.
It gives one community permanent control of government.
It makes respect for differences unnecessary for cooperation.

why.It can remove every conflict once and fo: This wrongly assumes that conflict can be permanently solved.
why.It gives one community permanent control: This confuses democracy with permanent control by one community.
why.It makes respect for differences unneces: This wrongly assumes that negotiation works without mutual respect.

activities.explanation: Democracy supports negotiation; respect can be learned, but conflict never fully ends.

lessons.title: Dignity and freedom of citizens

activities.prompt: How can democracy help every citizen feel respected and free?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: What makes democracy successful?
activities.body: Democracy works best when it protects each person's dignity and freedom. Respect and freedom are important bases of democracy. However, recognising equality does not always mean women receive respect. Democracy can strengthen claims of disadvantaged and discriminated castes. Its ongoing examination means it keeps checking how well it works. This examination never ends because new tests keep appearing. Complaints can show that people can question power holders.
keyPoints: Democracy promotes individual dignity and freedom.
Respect and freedom are important bases.
Democracy keeps producing new tests.
activities.explanation: Democracy always needs attention to dignity, freedom, and equal respect.

activities.prompt: A group complains that a leader ignores people. What does this tell us about democracy?
steps: People can complain because they are able to question power holders.
The complaint shows that people have become aware.
Democracy promotes dignity and freedom, so questioning power holders is important.
Democracy's examination never ends, so more tests can follow.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Why democracy must keep examining itself
activities.body: Equality needs careful attention. Recognising equality does not mean women are always treated with respect. This shows why democracy must keep examining itself. Its examination never ends because it keeps producing new tests. Complaints about democracy matter. They show that people have become aware and can question power holders. These ideas help you judge democracy by dignity, freedom, and equal respect.
keyPoints: Recognising equality does not always bring respect.
Democracy's examination keeps producing new tests.
Complaints show that people can question power holders.
activities.explanation: Keeping questions alive helps democracy protect dignity, freedom, and equal respect.

activities.prompt: Which two things are important bases of democracy?
options: Caste and equality
Complaints and questions
Respect and freedom
Tests and examinations
activities.explanation: Respect and freedom are important bases of democracy.

activities.prompt: Democracy is especially successful at promoting individual dignity and freedom.
activities.explanation: Yes. Democracy is especially successful when it promotes individual dignity and freedom.

activities.prompt: Democracy in India has strengthened the claims of ______ and discriminated castes.
activities.hint: Name the group whose claims have been strengthened.
activities.explanation: Good work. Democracy in India has strengthened the claims of disadvantaged and discriminated castes.

activities.prompt: Match each idea with its meaning from the lesson.
pairs: A system that promotes dignity and freedom
Signs that people question power holders
activities.explanation: You matched each idea with the correct meaning. These connections show democracy's main strengths.

activities.prompt: People complain that women are not treated with respect. What can this show?
options: Recognition guarantees equal respect.
People can question power holders.
Power holders cannot be questioned.
Democracy has reached its last test.
activities.explanation: Complaints show that people are aware and able to question power holders. Equality does not always mean equal respect.

activities.prompt: Which statement best explains why democracy's examination never ends?
options: It stops after equality is recognised.
It stays unchanged after its first test.
It ends when all complaints disappear.
It keeps producing new tests.
activities.explanation: Democracy's examination never ends because it keeps producing new tests.

activities.prompt: Residents can complain about leaders. What does this show about democracy?
options: People can question power holders and stay aware.
People believe complaints will solve every problem.
People have stopped questioning those in power.
People think democracy no longer needs testing.

why.People believe complaints will solve eve: Wrong: this mistake treats complaints as proof that every problem will be solved.
why.People have stopped questioning those in: Wrong: this mistake thinks questioning ends when complaints begin.
why.People think democracy no longer needs t: Wrong: this mistake believes democracy has already passed every test.

activities.explanation: Right: complaints show people can question power holders.

activities.prompt: A school says everyone is equal, but some girls are not respected. What should we understand?
options: Recognising equality does not always bring respect.
Equality always means everyone receives equal respect.
Girls do not need respect once rights are equal.
Equality and respect must always be exactly the same.

why.Equality always means everyone receives: Wrong: this mistake assumes equal rights guarantee equal treatment.
why.Girls do not need respect once rights ar: Wrong: this mistake thinks girls need less respect than others.
why.Equality and respect must always be exac: Wrong: this mistake treats equality and respect as one idea.

activities.explanation: Right: recognising equality does not mean women are always treated with respect.

activities.prompt: A discriminated caste uses democracy to demand a fair share. What can democracy strengthen?
options: The claims of disadvantaged and discriminated castes.
The power of those who already dominate.
The right to ignore every unfair decision.
The separation between citizens and leaders.

Wrong: this mistake thinks democracy only strengthens existing power.
why.The right to ignore every unfair decisio: Wrong: this mistake believes fairness means refusing every decision.
why.The separation between citizens and lead: Wrong: this mistake separates citizens' rights from democratic strength.

activities.explanation: Right: democracy strengthened these groups' claims in India.

activities.prompt: A democracy solves one problem, but another problem appears. What should we expect next?
options: Democracy will keep producing new tests.
Democracy will stop testing itself after this problem.
Democracy has already passed its final examination.
New problems will make democracy unnecessary.

why.Democracy will stop testing itself after: Wrong: this mistake thinks one solved problem ends all testing.
why.Democracy has already passed its final e: Wrong: this mistake treats the latest success as the final test.
why.New problems will make democracy unneces: Wrong: this mistake thinks new problems remove democracy's value.

activities.explanation: Right: democracy's examination never ends because new tests keep coming.

activities.prompt: Citizens speak freely and are treated with respect. What result can follow?
options: Democracy can promote individual dignity and freedom.
Democracy can end all future tests.
Democracy can make complaints impossible.
Democracy can stop people questioning leaders.

Wrong: this mistake thinks solving problems ends democracy's tests.
why.Democracy can make complaints impossible: Wrong: this mistake thinks respect prevents citizens from complaining.
why.Democracy can stop people questioning le: Wrong: this mistake believes freedom stops people questioning leaders.

activities.explanation: Right: democracy especially succeeds at promoting individual dignity and freedom.

activities.context: A town has introduced democratic meetings so residents can discuss local issues and vote on decisions. When residents disagree, they use the meetings to settle the dispute rather than abandoning the process. After one decision creates problems, the council allows further discussion and another vote, making room for correction. The meetings offer conditions for achieving goals, but residents must actively use them if their hopes for equality, dignity and better decisions are to be met.
activities.prompt: If residents stop attending the meetings and refuse to use the democratic process, what is the most likely result?
options: Their goals are less likely to be achieved because they are not using the conditions democracy has created.
All their goals will be achieved automatically because the meetings already exist.
They will no longer need to participate because democratic conditions remove citizens’ responsibilities.
Their hopes for equality, dignity and better decisions will be met without any further effort.

why.All their goals will be achieved automat: This confuses opportunities created by democracy with guaranteed results.
why.They will no longer need to participate: Democracy still requires citizens to participate and use its conditions.
why.Their hopes for equality, dignity and be: The expected benefits of democracy do not arise without citizen action.

activities.explanation: Democratic conditions do not produce goals without citizens using them.

activities.context: A town has introduced democratic meetings so residents can discuss local issues and vote on decisions. When residents disagree, they use the meetings to settle the dispute rather than abandoning the process. After one decision creates problems, the council allows further discussion and another vote, making room for correction. The meetings offer conditions for achieving goals, but residents must actively use them if their hopes for equality, dignity and better decisions are to be met.
activities.prompt: If the council refuses to reconsider the decision that caused problems, what is the most likely consequence?
options: A chance to correct the mistake is lost.
Equality among citizens will automatically be guaranteed.
The method for resolving conflicts will become less useful.
Democracy will have achieved the citizens’ goals by itself.

why.Equality among citizens will automatical: Refusing to reconsider does not guarantee equality.
why.The method for resolving conflicts will: Without discussion, disagreements may not be resolved through the democratic method.
why.Democracy will have achieved the citizen: Democracy cannot achieve goals without citizens using the conditions it creates.

activities.explanation: Refusing reconsideration removes an opportunity to correct an error.

activities.prompt:
Assertion (A): Democracy is expected to improve the quality of decision-making.
Reason (R): More than a hundred countries claim and practise some form of democratic politics.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
activities.explanation: Both statements are true, but the number of countries practising democracy does not explain why decision-making improves.

activities.prompt:
Assertion (A): Democracy cannot achieve goals by itself.
Reason (R): Citizens must use the conditions created by democracy to achieve their goals.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
activities.explanation: The requirement for citizens to use democratic conditions explains why democracy cannot achieve goals by itself.

activities.prompt: How does democracy create conditions for achieving citizens’ goals, and what must citizens do?
activities.answer: Democracy can create conditions in which citizens can pursue their goals. It is expected to promote equality, enhance each person’s dignity, improve decision-making, provide a way to resolve conflicts, and allow mistakes to be corrected. More than a hundred countries claim and practise some form of democratic politics, although their social situations, economic achievements and cultures differ. However, democracy is only one form of government and cannot achieve goals by itself. Citizens must use the conditions it creates, because democratic opportunities do not produce desired outcomes automatically.
points: Identifies the expected benefits of democracy.
Notes that democracies differ in social situations, economic achievements and cultures.
Explains that democracy is only one form of government.
States that citizens must use the conditions democracy creates.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: After residents asked to discuss how local services should be improved, the council invited them to an open public debate. It followed accepted procedures and provided information about the work of its office. Some residents said the delay showed that democracy was inefficient. Others replied that the process gave citizens a way to participate, allowed them to examine decisions, and helped make the final decision acceptable and effective. This ability to check the process is transparency.
activities.prompt: If the council skipped an accepted procedure so that it could decide faster, what problem would this most likely create?
options: It would weaken citizens' ability to check how the government decided.
Skipping a procedure would automatically make the decision corrupt.
Citizens would lose their right to information about government work.
The government would no longer be legitimate because it had acted quickly.

why.Skipping a procedure would automatically: Skipping a procedure does not automatically cause corruption.
why.Citizens would lose their right to infor: One skipped procedure does not cancel citizens' right to information.
why.The government would no longer be legiti: Speed alone does not remove the government's legitimacy as the people's own government.

activities.explanation: Democratic procedures allow citizens to examine how decisions were made.

activities.context: After residents asked to discuss how local services should be improved, the council invited them to an open public debate. It followed accepted procedures and provided information about the work of its office. Some residents said the delay showed that democracy was inefficient. Others replied that the process gave citizens a way to participate, allowed them to examine decisions, and helped make the final decision acceptable and effective. This ability to check the process is transparency.
activities.prompt: Residents accept a democratic decision after participating, but its later results are mixed. What is the best assessment?
options: The government can remain legitimate and answerable even when results are mixed.
A mixed record proves that democratic procedures always fail.
Public acceptance means that every democratic outcome will be effective.
The government should stop checking its work because citizens already accepted it.

why.A mixed record proves that democratic pr: A mixed record does not show that procedures always fail.
why.Public acceptance means that every democ: Acceptance may support effectiveness, but it does not guarantee every result.
why.The government should stop checking its: An accountable government must remain answerable to the people after a decision.

activities.explanation: Democracies have a mixed performance record, but this does not remove their legitimacy.

activities.prompt:
Assertion (A): Transparency allows citizens to examine how a democratic decision was made.
Reason (R): Democratic decision-making follows accepted norms and procedures that citizens can examine.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
activities.explanation: The reason explains transparency because examining accepted procedures enables citizens to check how decisions were made.

activities.prompt:
Assertion (A): Democratic governments may take more time before making decisions.
Reason (R): Democratic government is legitimate because it is the people's own government.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
activities.explanation: Both statements are true, but legitimacy does not explain why democratic procedures may take more time.

activities.prompt: Explain the difference between transparency and accountability in a democratic government.
activities.answer: Transparency means that citizens can examine how a decision was made. Accountability means that the government follows procedures and is accountable to the people. Transparency therefore focuses on making the decision-making process visible, while accountability focuses on the government's duty to justify its actions and remain responsible to citizens. Both are important because citizens should be able to check decisions and influence decisions that affect them. Citizens should also have access to information about government work so that they can evaluate whether the government is acting responsibly.
points: Transparency allows citizens to examine decisions.
Accountability requires procedures and responsibility to the people.
Citizens should have information and participation rights.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: After a country became a democracy, its leaders hoped this would lead to economic development. Many democracies did not fulfil that expectation, while dictatorships had a slightly higher rate of economic growth overall. A student therefore wondered whether the country should reject democracy. Another student replied that the growth result alone was not enough to do so, because economic development depends on several different factors.
activities.prompt: If the leaders want to understand why economic development has been disappointing, what should they do?
options: Investigate the different factors affecting development instead of assuming that democracy alone will solve the problem.
Reject democracy immediately because dictatorships have shown a slightly higher overall growth rate.
Assume that every democracy will eventually grow faster than every dictatorship.
Use the overall growth comparison as the only basis for deciding whether democracy is desirable.

why.Reject democracy immediately because dic: The growth result alone is not a reason to reject democracy.
why.Assume that every democracy will eventua: The facts do not support assuming that every democracy will grow faster.
why.Use the overall growth comparison as the: The result should prompt concern, not become the only basis for a decision.

activities.explanation: This follows the fact that development depends on several different factors.

activities.context: After a country became a democracy, its leaders hoped this would lead to economic development. Many democracies did not fulfil that expectation, while dictatorships had a slightly higher rate of economic growth overall. A student therefore wondered whether the country should reject democracy. Another student replied that the growth result alone was not enough to do so, because economic development depends on several different factors.
activities.prompt: What should citizens reasonably expect from democracy in relation to economic growth?
options: They should expect it to avoid falling behind dictatorships, without treating it as a guarantee of development.
They should expect it to guarantee the highest development rate in every situation.
They should expect it to grow more slowly than every dictatorship because it is democratic.
They should expect it to replace the need to consider other factors affecting development.

why.They should expect it to guarantee the h: A guarantee is stronger than what the facts support.
why.They should expect it to grow more slowl: The facts suggest a slight overall difference, not universal slower growth.
why.They should expect it to replace the nee: Other factors still matter because development depends on several factors.

activities.explanation: This combines the expectation about relative growth with the limits of democracy.

activities.prompt:
Assertion (A): Dictatorships had a slightly higher rate of economic growth overall.
Reason (R): Many democracies did not fulfil the expectation of economic development.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
activities.explanation: Both statements are true, but the second does not explain the overall growth-rate comparison.

activities.prompt:
Assertion (A): Democracy cannot be treated as a guarantee of economic development.
Reason (R): Economic development depends on several different factors.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
activities.explanation: The presence of several factors explains why democratic government alone cannot guarantee development.

activities.prompt: Explain why the growth result alone should not be used to reject democracy.
activities.answer: The growth comparison gives a reason for concern because many democracies did not fulfil the expectation of economic development, and dictatorships had a slightly higher overall growth rate. However, this result alone is not a reason to reject democracy. Economic development depends on several different factors, so the comparison cannot be treated as proof that democracy alone explains the outcome. Democracy cannot be treated as a guarantee of economic development, but it can reasonably be expected to avoid falling behind dictatorships in economic growth. The result should therefore lead to careful consideration rather than an automatic rejection of democracy.
points: Many democracies did not fulfil the development expectation.
Dictatorships had only a slightly higher overall growth rate.
Development depends on several different factors.
The result alone does not justify rejecting democracy.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Rina lives in Bangladesh, where more than half the population lives in poverty. She cannot meet basic needs such as food, clothing, housing, education and health. Although every person has equal weight when electing representatives, democracy has not been very successful in reducing economic inequalities. A small number of ultra-rich people receive a highly disproportionate share of wealth and income, while bottom incomes decline. Poor people form a large proportion of voters.
activities.prompt: Suppose political participation becomes more equal while the distribution of wealth and income does not change. What is likely to happen?
options: Economic inequality can continue growing despite greater political equality.
The economic gap must disappear because votes are equally weighted.
Bottom incomes must rise because the number of voters is large.
Basic needs will become easier to meet solely because voting is equal.

why.The economic gap must disappear because: Equal voting weight does not guarantee an equal economic outcome.
why.Bottom incomes must rise because the num: A large number of voters does not itself raise poor incomes.
why.Basic needs will become easier to meet s: Greater political equality alone does not ensure that basic needs are met.

activities.explanation: Political equality does not automatically change wealth and income.

activities.context: Rina lives in Bangladesh, where more than half the population lives in poverty. She cannot meet basic needs such as food, clothing, housing, education and health. Although every person has equal weight when electing representatives, democracy has not been very successful in reducing economic inequalities. A small number of ultra-rich people receive a highly disproportionate share of wealth and income, while bottom incomes decline. Poor people form a large proportion of voters.
activities.prompt: Rina’s income is among those at the bottom and continues to decline. What is the most likely consequence?
options: Her difficulty meeting basic needs may increase.
Her vote will automatically carry more weight because she is poorer.
The wealth share of the ultra-rich will automatically become more equal.
Economic inequality must disappear because she is a voter.

why.Her vote will automatically carry more w: Being poorer does not change a voter’s equal electoral weight.
why.The wealth share of the ultra-rich will: Declining bottom incomes do not automatically alter the wealth distribution.
why.Economic inequality must disappear becau: Being a voter does not automatically remove economic inequality.

activities.explanation: Declining bottom incomes can make basic needs harder to meet.

activities.prompt:
Assertion (A): Democratic elections do not automatically ensure that wealth and income are distributed more equally.
Reason (R): Economic inequalities can grow even while political participation becomes more equal.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
activities.explanation: The reason directly explains why political equality does not automatically reduce economic inequality.

boss.title: Chapter challenge: Outcomes of Democracy

activities.title: Expected outcomes
activities.prompt: Which outcome is NOT an expected benefit of democracy?
options: Equality among all citizens
Greater dignity for each person
Better quality of decision-making
Permanent removal of social conflicts
activities.explanation: Democracy may promote equality, dignity and better decisions. It cannot permanently remove every social conflict.

activities.title: Democratic procedures
activities.prompt: Democratic governments take more time because they follow procedures before making decisions.
activities.explanation: Following procedures can make democratic decisions more acceptable and effective.

activities.title: Rules for decisions
activities.prompt: Democratic decision-making is based on accepted ______ and procedures.
activities.hint: These are shared rules for making decisions.
activities.explanation: Democratic decision-making uses accepted norms and procedures.

activities.title: Using democracy
activities.prompt: Put these steps in order.
items: Citizens work towards their own goals
activities.explanation: Democracy creates conditions. Citizens must then use them to work towards their goals.

activities.title: Development and democracy
activities.prompt: Which conclusion about democracy and economic development is stated in your book?
options: Democracy guarantees better development for every country
Many democracies did not fulfil the development expectation
Dictatorships always achieved a higher economic growth rate
Economic development depends on a single clear factor
activities.explanation: Many democracies did not fulfil this expectation. The growth result alone is not a reason to reject democracy.

activities.title: No automatic promise
activities.prompt: Democracy cannot be treated as a ______ of economic development.
activities.hint: This word means a sure promise of success.
activities.explanation: Democracy may help create conditions, but it cannot guarantee economic development.

activities.title: Majority and minority
activities.prompt: How should a majority act in a democracy?
options: Leave the minority outside to protect majority rule
Work with minorities to represent the general view
Give one religious community permanent control over government
Let one language group decide every government matter
activities.explanation: A majority must work with the minority. Majority rule must not become control by one community.

activities.title: Two kinds of equality
activities.prompt: Which statement about equality in democracies is correct?
options: Political equality always prevents every economic inequality
Wealthy groups receive more weight when electing leaders
Economic inequalities can grow as political equality grows
Poor voters receive less weight when choosing representatives
activities.explanation: Democracies are based on political equality. Economic inequalities can still grow while participation becomes more equal.
